_what: The exact Hyperliquid /exchange POST bodies this build signs, frozen. Replayed by crates/bridges/hyperliquid/tests/signed_payload_fixtures.rs, which carries the full rationale.
_property: STABILITY, not correctness — with ONE exception named below. These bytes were RECORDED from this implementation, not ported from a venue SDK vector: neither official Hyperliquid SDK publishes one for usdClassTransfer or approveBuilderFee (measured 2026-09-14). They prove the signed payload did not change; they do not prove it was ever right.
_the_one_exception: l1_limit_order_no_vault reproduces the official Rust SDK's test_limit_order_action_hashing inputs exactly — its key, its action, its nonce 1583838 — so the signature inside that payload IS the SDK's published mainnet vector and is checked against it. That one case is a correctness anchor; the other five are not.
_authority: The frozen side wins. A mismatch means a source key or an EIP-712 type string moved: restore the source. Editing this file to match makes a protocol break permanent and silent, which is the exact failure the test exists to prevent. There is deliberately no regenerator.
_inputs: Signed with the official Rust SDK's public test key (e908f8…688e — no funds, no account). User-signed cases use nonce 1700000000123; L1 cases use the SDK's own 1583838. RFC-6979 ECDSA makes every byte, signature included, deterministic.
_fields: `payload` is the exact UTF-8 request body, compared byte-for-byte. `digest` is the EIP-712 message the signature was produced over — present only for the user-signed pair, and the only thing that moves if an eip712.rs type string is edited. `primary_type` is the hashed type string itself, matched as raw text so a new user-signed action cannot ship without a frozen digest.
_one_exception_to_byte_for_byte: The two l1_limit_order_* payloads are compared byte-for-byte FIRST and, only if that fails, re-judged with every object's keys sorted. Their JSON key order is not this repo's to pin: src/transport.rs's exchange_body returns a serde_json::Value, and serde_json::Map is a BTreeMap (sorted) or an IndexMap (declaration order) depending on whether anything else in the build graph enables serde_json/preserve_order — datafusion-physical-plan does, so `cargo test -p vike-hyperliquid` alone and the full roster lane emit DIFFERENT bytes from identical source. The key order recorded below is the sorted one. Nothing else is relaxed: a changed serde rename moves a key, a changed signature moves a value, and neither survives the sorting. The SIGNED bytes are unaffected — the L1 signature is msgpack over the Action struct, computed before to_value is called, and the user-signed digests are EIP-712 over typed fields with no JSON in the preimage. crates/bridges/hyperliquid/tests/signed_payload_fixtures.rs's ORDER_UNSTABLE_CASES is the declared set and carries the argument.
